title: A common denominator lies in the Jacobson radicals
statement: Let A be a commutative domain (a ring with no zero divisors) with fraction field K (a field containing A in which every element is a quotient of elements of A). Let B_1, ..., B_r be subrings of K that are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], of Krull dimension 1 [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], semilocal (having finitely many maximal ideals) domains with fraction field K. Assume that each canonical map A \otimes B_i \to K is surjective. Then there exists a nonzero f\in A such that f^{-1} belongs to the Jacobson radical (the intersection of all maximal ideals) of every B_i.

proof.text: Pass from each B_i to its integral closure C_i in K. The conductor theorem [lem-sc-semilocal-dim-one-conductor] provides semilocal Dedekind and fraction-field instances, dimension one, and the conductor power property for C_i. Tensor surjectivity passes to C_i: map the right tensor factor by B_i to C_i, and the scalar-tower identity proves that the new multiplication map composed with this tensor map is the old multiplication map.

Use [lem-sc-semilocal-dedekind-dvr-reduction] for each C_i. Index the resulting DVRs by the finite dependent sum of i and the maximal ideals of C_i. Their algebras into K are exactly the canonical localization algebras in that theorem. Tensor surjectivity passes to each localization by the same tensor-factor map. Fix the canonical integer algebra structure on these localizations, avoiding the competing localization-derived integer algebra instance.

For one DVR D, use its normalized multiplicative valuation v:K to the multiplicative integers with zero, as supplied by the DVR convention [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Suppose every image of a in A has value at most one. Every image of d in D has value at most one (Mathlib HeightOneSpectrum.valuation_le_one). Tensor induction, using multiplication and the nonarchimedean sum inequality from [lem-sc-dvr-valuation-arithmetic], then gives v(p(z)) at most one for every tensor z. The normalized valuation is surjective (Mathlib HeightOneSpectrum.valuation_surjective); take k with v(k)=exp(1)>1. Tensor surjectivity supplies z with p(z)=k, a contradiction. Hence some a in A has value greater than one, and is nonzero because the value at zero is zero. This proves the single-DVR base case directly, without the subring-specific statement module.

Induct over a finite set of valuations. For the empty set take 1. Given nonzero x with v_j(x)>1 at the preceding places, keep x if it also works at the new place i. Otherwise v_i(x) is at most one; choose y with v_i(y)>1 by the preceding base case. For each preceding j choose n_j with v_j(x) to the power n_j greater than max(1,v_j(y)); this is Archimedean growth in the multiplicative integers with zero, with the zero case handled separately. Set N=1+sum n_j. Then N is at least every n_j and powers of a value greater than one increase. Thus v_j(x^N)>max(1,v_j(y)). At the new place v_i(x^N) is at most one and smaller than v_i(y). The unequal-value sum formula [lem-sc-dvr-valuation-arithmetic] gives v_j(x^N+y)=v_j(x^N)>1 at every preceding place and v_i(x^N+y)=v_i(y)>1 at the new place. The latter also proves that x^N+y is nonzero.

The resulting f has v_j(f)>1 at all localizations. Its inverse has value less than one. The Mathlib lifting statement [lem-sc-dvr-nonnegative-valuation-in-ring] produces an element d of each DVR with image f^{-1}; HeightOneSpectrum.valuation_lt_one_iff_mem puts d in its maximal ideal. The radical-membership equivalence [lem-sc-semilocal-dedekind-dvr-reduction] now gives c_i in the Jacobson radical of C_i with image f^{-1}. This c_i is nonzero by injectivity and f nonzero. Apply [lem-sc-semilocal-dim-one-conductor] to c_i and 1 to obtain positive n_i and b_i in B_i with image f^{-n_i}. Set P=product n_i, positive also for the empty family. Write P=n_i k_i. The element b_i^{k_i} has image f^{-P} and maps to c_i^P in C_i by injectivity. Since P>0, c_i^P remains in the Jacobson radical of C_i. Integral lying-over [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over], in Mathlib maximal-ideal form Ideal.exists_ideal_over_maximal_of_isIntegral, lifts every maximal ideal of B_i to one of C_i with that contraction. Therefore b_i^{k_i} belongs to every maximal ideal of B_i. Return f^P; its image has inverse f^{-P} and f^P is nonzero.

split_report.summary: Expanded Stacks 09N5 into the integral-closure/conductor reduction, the semilocal-Dedekind to DVR reduction, and the finite-valuation induction. Added statement-only interfaces for the non-elementary conductor, localization, one-DVR base case, and valuation-arithmetic facts.
